note: Tirumular says the garb is useless to those of petty knowledge and the good attain grace without it; Thirikonar's kings of sham silence, who claim detachment, are to be sent away while the true owners of silence (2226) are told the Siva-substance. Both judge the pose by the knowledge behind it.
audit_text_issue: 2233 breaks off mid-unit (ஞானப்).

note: Tirumular nurtured the body because without it true knowledge cannot be won; Mounachiddhar's company ate kalpa and grew the body in the same cave where they saw the supreme open. Both make the lasting body a means of the vision, not its enemy.

One poet laments that by not keeping his eyes on the nose-tip his body was spoiled and his understanding lost; Mounachiddhar's Siddhars learned the nose-tip gaze and with it cut off desire. The same practice, its loss and its keeping.

Tirumular turns the one who blazes at the root opening upward with the breath joined; Mounachiddhar seizes the breath and raises the fire at the root. The same coupling of breath and root-fire, here told as a thing the company has done.

The Kural's bird leaves its egg or nest empty, an image of how slight the bond of body and life is; Punnakku's chick lies whole in the egg, an image of the life complete within the body-shirt. The same egg, used once for leaving and once for what is already inside.

The Kural asks whether the life lodging in a corner of the body has found no home of its own; Punnakku says the body and even the loincloth are on loan. Both make the body a lent or rented place, not the self's possession.

The Naladiyar's drummers beat three times and the dying carry the dead; Punnakku's mourners beat drums and weep without counting their own days. Both use the funeral drum to show that those who mourn are on the same road.

Both call the body a pot filled with wind and filth. Pattinathar's poet loved it and carried it about; Punnakku names it a saltless false nest, built by the five to rule, so the same pot is a confession in one and a diagnosis in the other.

Tirumular says to teach only those of ripe mind; Punnakku says teaching the willing is always fine and teaching the wicked brings ruin. The same rule of fitness, Punnakku adding the danger of breaking it.

Tirumular's formless Lord cannot be reached by anyone without the guru; Punnakku's forest-dweller of golden austerities cannot find it without a guru. Both make the guru necessary even where effort is complete.
audit_text_issue: 2262: repeated காட்டில் may be a copying slip.

note: Pattinathar lists observances, Vedas, fire rites, japa, ash and sandal and the pujas of every watch and calls all of it pretence; Punnakku compresses the list to smearing, talk, puja and hand-waving and calls it a mark for mockery.

Kanjamalai calls the inquiry of stainless jnana-Vedanta the one essence; Pattiragiriyar asks when he will leave all Vedanta and the Veda behind and stay alone in absorption. If both mean Vedanta as a body of teaching, the one keeps what the other discards; if Kanjamalai means the knowledge and Pattiragiriyar the texts, they agree. The tension holds on the first reading.

2270 makes the world a dream and a conjuror's show produced by the inner faculties; 2291 says no one can push the faculties' play away, that bondage is being coupled to it, and that the self-light appears within it. The second stanza keeps the first's doctrine and removes its hope of stopping the show.
audit_text_issue: 2270 last line (அன்று தோன்றி விட்டாலது சூட்சானு கூலம்) is obscure.

note: The Kural says that giving up insatiable craving at once gives a nature that never shifts; Kanjamalai says that when desire is thrown out root and bundle, the dissolution of mind joins of itself. Both make the positive state follow immediately and without further effort from the removal of craving.

Tirumular's true guru, by giving his feet, grants self-knowledge, brings the soul beyond the tattvas and quells the bonds; Kanjamalai says the heaps of tattvas and the rites are nothing and that seeing the guru's feet is when it becomes known. The feet do in both what the tattva-lists cannot.

Tirumular says the Lord's servants, the Siva-yogis and the eminent do not want ritual works, they want love; Kanjamalai asks what the rites called sastras of attainment are and answers with unforgetting devotion and the guru's feet. Both set bhakti against rite from inside a tradition that prescribes rite.

Tirumular's Lord is far off yet near to those who love well; Kanjamalai says there are no far distances, that grasping him by effort is great trouble, and that trusting the guru's word brings one to the limit. In both the distance is not spatial and is closed by trust, not by reaching.

Sangili's five persons join to rule and build the body as the Gingee fort; Kanjamalai's body comes from ego-impurity and five sit in it and work by rule. The five (elements or senses) govern the body in both, and both poets call the account a secret told plainly.

Tirumular's ritualist eats bitter things while ghee, milk and curd stand at hand; Kanjamalai says do not drink poison while the nectar of jnana is there. The same figure of the worthless chosen over the precious at hand, Tirumular's for the karmi beside the jnani, Kanjamalai's for display and lust beside knowledge.

Tirumular says that though many speak of the things to join with the Pure One, the one who conquers the senses and quickly ends dispute knows him; Kanjamalai says do not dispute saying 'I', do not throw out arguments. Both make the end of argument a condition of knowing, not a result.
audit_text_issue: 2277 second half (ஊனென்ற பாசம் மாறாதே ... உன்னாணை) is obscure.

note: Tirumular's knowers perceive Siva's fragrance in the soul 'steady as a painting'; Kanjamalai says stay still like a picture and utter nothing. The painted figure is the still yogi in both, and both pair the stillness with silence.

The Kural says what is not yours will not stay however guarded and what is yours will not leave though thrown away; Kanjamalai says do not push away what has come and do not crave what has not. The Kural's chapter is on ஊழ், fate; Kanjamalai draws from the same fact the yogi's equanimity rather than a doctrine of fate.

Sivavakkiyar's book-carriers babble lies and do not know where one dies and is born; Kanjamalai says to cross the delusion of learning and destroy the dross of 'we have learned it all'. Both aim at the pride of the learned, not at learning as such, and both set an inner knowledge against it.
audit_text_issue: 2281 has no finite verb and runs into 2282.

note: Pattiragiriyar asks when he will see the waste mind that wanders by the five senses' paths burn and fall; Kanjamalai tells the listener to catch the thought that runs about and set it in the open space of nada's end. The same running mind, to be burnt in the one and lodged in the other.

Tirumular's soul, freed of the malas, sees itself and becomes Hara, beyond the tattvas, which he calls Vedanta's truth; Kanjamalai's egoist soul is destroyed by ignorance, reaches awareness by tapas and becomes Shakti's form by holding the state. Both run from the bound soul to divine form, Tirumular's ending in Siva and Kanjamalai's in Shakti.
audit_text_issue: tirumanthiram:2401 line 4 வினாவு may be a misprint for விரவு.

note: Tirumular's Siva-yoga is to know the conscient and the non-conscient, enter the yoga of tapas and become one's own light; Kanjamalai's Siva-yoga is to stay alone and stand as oneself alone in an impermanent body. Both define Siva-yoga by a state of the self rather than by posture or breath.

The Kural says the moment attachment ends it cuts off births; Kanjamalai says give no room to desire, do not get bound in the body's pains, do not take birth again. Both make the end of craving and the end of birth one event; Kanjamalai adds the guru's feet as the thing to hold instead.

Sivavakkiyar counts the flowers he threw, the mantras he recited into the void and the times he circled Siva's temples; Kanjamalai calls crores of austerities and the japa recited round the temple a toil of births. Both count the acts to show that counting them is all they amount to.
audit_text_issue: siddhar:2290 அமலங்கள் read as மலங்கள் is uncertain.

note: Tirumular says those who do great tapas without forgetting win the greatness of ending birth; Kanjamalai says crores upon crores of tapas, with temple japa, are a toil of births and the defilements of sorrow. If தவங்கள் in 2290 means tapas as such, the two claims about what tapas does to birth are opposite; if it means only the ritual austerities counted and performed, Tirumular's unforgetting tapas is a different thing.
audit_text_issue: siddhar:2290 அமலங்கள் read as மலங்கள் is uncertain.

note: The Tirumanthiram names a Kanjamalaiyan among those who examined the root chariyai, the outward service of the Lord that is 'the life of pure Saivam'; the song under Kanjamalai Siddhar's name calls the japa recited round the temple a toil of births. If the two names are one person, the texts give him opposite valuations of temple service; if not, the tension is between the lineage's founder and a later namesake. Either way the claim that chariyai is the life of Saivam and the claim that temple rounds are a burden of births do not stand together.
audit_text_issue: 2290: the sense of அமலங்கள் and பாடான பவங்கள் is uncertain.

note: 2268 commands the listener to utter the rare name of Siva among four imperatives; 2292 closes the song by making the form of the name itself the attainment and its clarified seeking release. The name that was one practice at the opening is the whole at the close.

The Puranamalai says that those who say 'breath', 'heart', 'the release called silence' and 'speech' do not know the Lord's name; Kanjamalai says the form of the name is itself attainment and its seeking release. Both make the name the thing the methods miss, on the reading that நாம சொரூபம் is the Lord's name; if it is Vedanta's name-and-form the two verses are about different things.
audit_text_issue: 2292 flagged uncertain; நாம/நேம சொரூபம் ambiguous.

note: Both set Kalangi and Bogar in one line of teachers descending from Tirumular: Tirumular names Bhoga Devar among those who came from Kalangar, and Nondi's roll call runs Tirumular, Kalangi, Bogar.

Sivavakkiyar gives chariyai and kiriyai their own fruits, salokam and samipam, within a graded scheme where all four paths reach something; Nondi sets the two aside altogether and touches yoga as the means beyond them, with no fruit assigned to what he left.
audit_text_issue: உரியா தீதம்வெளிப்பட் டங்கு appears garbled (உரிய அதீதம்).

note: Both put the goal beyond the first two paths: Arunagiri's supreme light cannot be reached by those joined to chariyai and kiriyai, and Nondi leaves them to touch the foot of yoga and finds a state he cannot tell.

Both place the Lord at a point measured from the nose-tip and beyond speech: Tirumular puts his dwelling a few finger-breadths from it, which the Veda shrinks from telling; Nondi sees the teacher's dance in the light between the eyes at the nose-tip and falls into silence.
audit_text_issue: 2301: பரிசமுத்தே unclear.

note: Pattinathar's Arutpulambal says the Omkara itself perished with the ego, cut at the root; Nondi says that seeing what the pranava Om truly is brought him great good and ended the ego that says 'we'. They conflict if Pattinathar means Om is no means at all in the final state; if he means only that Om as sound dissolves there, Nondi's nadanta silence in 2312 says the same.

Both make Sathuragiri the siddhas' seat and a station on the way: Subramaniar Njanam tells the disciple to go to its summit and practise there; Nondi says he went there by the sky path and rejoiced among the siddhas of tapas.

Both credit the goddess Manonmani with giving the means: in Tirumular she wakes the sleeping yogi and gives the upaya; in Nondi it is by her grace that he knew the unknowable fullness and merged in it.

Pattinathar: the place where sound subsides is the light within Om, and that is the Brahman that stays without speaking; Nondi: he stayed in the state called the silence at the end of nada and saw the higher house. Both put the final silence where sound ends rather than in mere quiet.

Nondi's wicked 'chandalas' are company he forgot in order to find the fit vessel and join the worthy; the word marks conduct, not birth. The Kural redefines birth by conduct in the same way: having conduct is noble birth, failing in it low birth. The agreement holds if சண்டாளர் is read morally, as the stanza's contrast with பாத்திரம் suggests.

The salted pot (உப்பிட்ட பாண்டம்) for the body that dissolves: in the Meynjanap Pulambal it must break and take a womb again unless the Lord takes the speaker; in Nondi those who do not know the truth call it good and wander in bondage.
audit_text_issue: 2314: doubled வந்தவழி and செப்புக் குயமானார் look corrupt.

note: The body as a false hut or cage (பொய்க்கூடு): Arunagiri's speaker lives in the illusion that life in it is unshaken greatness; Nondi, certain it has no substance, fears and goes to a mountain cave to learn the way of Sivajnana.

Both start from the body of nine gates and make stilling or shutting them the condition of what follows: Tirumular's nine channels stilled in the one place, Nondi's gates closed before he goes through the great high path.
audit_text_issue: Tirumanthiram 658 line 4 (ஒன்பது காட்சி இலைபல வாமே, variant உலைநலம் ஆமே) is corrupt; Siddhar 2317 has a stray '.' in பெருவழி .ஊடுசென்று.

note: Sivavakkiyar seals the gates, five and four, with the final mudra and goes up the root channel past the lotus temple; Nondi realises the nine gates, closes them and goes through the great high path. The same body and the same closing before ascent.
audit_text_issue: 2317 has a stray mark in பெருவழி .ஊடு.

note: In 2301 the teacher's dance is seen in the light at the nose-tip, silently; 2318 moves the vision to the goddess Manonmani's seat and adds sound, the ringing of bells and the song of nada, before the dance is seen. Sight first, then sound and sight together.

Both say the open space is there to be seen and that the fault is in the seer: Tirumular's people do not open their eyes even when it dawns; Nondi asks whether those who take broad daylight for darkness have an eye of knowledge at all. In both the inner eye, not the light, is what is lacking.
audit_text_issue: 1687: உண்ணிமை obscure.

note: 2307 calls Nandisar 'my grandfather'; 2323 calls Tirumular 'our guru'. Together they claim the lineage Nandi, Tirumular, Nondi, so that the guru's saying quoted here is traced to the Tirumanthiram's author.
audit_text_issue: 2323: the quoted words மூல முதலி மொள்ளே are cipher or corrupt.

note: Pattinathar's heart puts away pride and fear and 'sleeps without sleeping' to gain happiness; Nondi, with 'he' and 'I' gone, stays in nishtai with an eye that does not sleep. The same wakeful absorption after the same ego-loss.

2315 is certain the body is a false unstable cage with no substance; 2324 keeps the fleshly body from perishing in nishtai and counts that among the attainments. The conflict stands if ஊனுடல் அழியாமல் claims the siddha's lasting body; if it means only that the body is kept through the trance, the two stanzas are about different moments.

2298 reports seeing the arising (உற்பனம்) of supreme consciousness as a gain; 2325 says every arising seen through the expansion of the one thing is empty imagination. The later stanza turns the earlier vision into something to be seen through.

Tirumular tells the practitioner to mark the adharas that have been taught and find the one letter above the fifty in the welling adhara; Kakapusundar says that whoever counts the supports as many and the places as twelve wastes away, since every place is the one crown. The conflict holds if 2328 attacks the doctrine of several centres, not merely talk without practice.
audit_text_issue: 2328 last line விடமுண்ட அண்டம் is unclear.

note: Tirumular makes the five letters the seat of Nandi and the chakra within which he sits; Kakapusundar says that in Brahman at the crown there are no mantras at all. The two clash if 2329 denies mantra as a way; if it only describes the state after arrival, Tirumular could agree.
2329 states that there are no mantras in Brahman; 2340 gives the reason: a mantra thought makes the mind two, and the way is the mind alone as one.

Both make the breath held high in the head the cure for ageing: Tirumular's two breaths set in the upper palate undo grey hair and wrinkles, Kakapusundar's breath climbing the nape path is the kalpa itself.

Both reduce the many methods to a few that matter: Tirumular's twenty thousand eight hundred kinds of karma, mantra and yoga give only toil and come down to four; Kakapusundar's sixty-four yogas ruin crores while raja yoga saves one.

Tirumular says that if the ordained temple pujas lapse disease grows, rain fails and kings weaken; Kakapusundar calls those who wander saying temple and tirtha thieves who fall like rootless trees. The conflict is over whether temple worship holds the world up or holds the seeker back; it stands on any reading of 2347.

Tirumular says pearl, ash, rice, flowers or sand can all be made the linga, the Father's body, by one who seeks to be saved; Kakapusundar says setting up a linga and plucking flowers for it offers a corpse and gets nothing. Both speak of the same act, outward linga worship; one makes it a way and the other a waste.
audit_text_issue: 2348 line 2 (பார்த்தீப லிங்கத்தைப் பணியாமற்றான்) and கத்தபம் are obscure; 1719 கொத்தும்அக்கொம்பு and கோமளம் unclear. The contrast does not depend on them.

note: Both move the linga inside: Tirumular makes the heart the temple and the soul the Sivalinga for those who are clear; Kakapusundar gives the Kailasa body to those who see within the Supreme with the mind rather than bowing to a set-up stone.
audit_text_issue: Siddhar 2348 line 2 பார்த்தீப and line 4 கத்தபம் are obscure.

note: Tirumular says that if the tip of the tongue is pressed up into the middle, soul and Siva dwell there and the flesh does not die for a hundred crore years; Kakapusundar says those who raised the tongue to the uvula got nothing, their eyes burst and the body went, and the mind alone should go there. Same place, opposite verdicts on the physical seal.

Both say the One itself stands as its opposites and its gods: Tirumular's Lord is the three lights in one, stands as Brahma and Vishnu, as space, light and darkness; Kakapusundar's one Brahman becomes good and evil, sun and moon, guru and disciple.

2349 condemns those who multiply gods and call this one guru and that one disciple instead of approaching Brahman; 2357 allows guru and disciple as marks the one Brahman takes. The pair is real as appearance, false as a second thing.

Tirumular's jnani is one who comes to see all the good books of the earth together with the way of silence and the end of the unwritten Veda; Kakapusundar says those locked onto the siddhas' books never see the egg. Tirumular includes books in what the jnani sees; Kakapusundar excludes them, so this narrows rather than contradicts.
Both say the ascetic's outward form without the inner strength is a disguise: the Kural's cow grazing in a tiger's skin, Kakapusundar's robed and staffed guru roaming like a dog.

The Kural says neither shaving nor matted hair is needed if one gives up what the world condemns; Kakapusundar mocks the ochre, the staff and the stoop as show. Both make the marks of renunciation worthless without the thing itself.

Both define the false guru by what he does with the teaching: Tirumular's has looked over mantra, yoga and jnana yet goes blind for the sake of food; Kakapusundar's gathers disciples to take their money and blames fate when his instruction fails.

Tirumular says those who know only bathing cannot join the Lord, who is in the minds of those whose knowledge is clear; Kakapusundar's tirtha is the Siva-Ganga at the crown and his flower the loving mind, and the clear (தெளிந்தவர்) are the true jnanis.
2348 rejects bathing a linga and offering plucked flowers; 2361 keeps bathing, name-mark and flower-offering as inner acts at the crown. The rite is not abolished but moved inside.
audit_text_issue: 2348 line 2 (பார்த்தீப லிங்கம், கத்தபம்) obscure; the bathing and flower lines are clear.

note: 2345 opens the forehead eye and finds the earth filled as one; 2362 says what it shows: the sights the ordinary eye cannot hold, and the seer standing as himself in every life.

Both say that at dissolution the works of Vishnu and Brahma sink back into the source: Tirumular's crop of the waste returns to the waste, Kakapusundar's Hari and Ayan and all lives are absorbed in the whole Brahman. Both also keep a remainder that does not perish: the waste itself, and the crow on Meru.
audit_text_issue: Siddhar 2373 lines 6-7 are grammatically loose (whether the crow form is taken once or at each re-creation).

note: Both make the linga something other than stone: Tirumular's soul is the Sivalinga in the temple of the heart, Kakapusundar's lingas are the central sky, Meru's summit, Shakti and breath, and samadhi, gathered into one supreme linga.

Arunagirinathar asks not to be the foolish yogi who, thinking impermanent flesh will last, holds the breath and eats herbs in austerity; Kakapusundar promises a body made rare and shadowless, the kaya siddhi, from the fire entering at the crown. The conflict holds if 2380 claims bodily permanence; if the rare body is a figure for freedom from the body, it weakens.

Both tie the eight siddhis to the breath mastered in the central way: Tirumular's come through eightfold yoga when the fire at the root drives the sun and lets the moon drink, Kakapusundar's dance when the breath merges and subsides in Brahman and the body has become rare.

Both promise undimmed youth from the inner practice: Tirumular's breaths set in the upper palate turn grey hair back and make one a child, Kakapusundar's great ones who saw silence before thirty stay young.

2353 tells the disciple to eat the karunelli and the white snake for a deathless head and leg; 2383 says there is no kalpa of plant or root and the body becomes firm only through absorption in Brahman. The conflict is real if 2353 is taken plainly; the tradition escapes it by reading its herb and snake as cipher for inner substances, which 2383 would then be stating openly.

Both displace the kalpa herb with an inner act: Tirumular says praising the Lord night and morning makes the body as if transmuted by the herb, Kakapusundar that the body grows firm in Brahman and no plant or root kalpa exists.
audit_text_issue: 293 lines 1-2 (பல்லி யுடையார் பாம்பரிந்து உண்கின்றார்) are obscure.

note: Both deny caste to the knower: for Tirumular those who set Nandi in love by knowledge have no caste, no stain and no pride; Kakapusundar's only clan is seed, all lives having arisen alike from Brahman.

The Naladiyar says good caste and bad caste are empty words and lineage is made by tapas, learning and effort; Kakapusundar says caste is spoken only by the unseeing and all are born of the same seed. Both empty birth-caste, though the Naladiyar puts conduct in its place and Kakapusundar puts common origin.

2348 scorns those who set up a linga, bathe it and offer flowers; 2394 prescribes pooja to the god at the three sandhis with the chitta one. 2395 shows the sandhis are the three lights, so the pooja kept is inner and the rejection of 2348 is of the outer act only.
audit_text_issue: 2348 line 2 (பார்த்தீப லிங்கத்தைப் பணியா மற்றான்) and கத்தபம் are obscure, but the scorn for bathing and flower offering is clear.

note: 2394 prescribes pooja at dawn, dusk and noon; 2395 defines those three times as sun, moon and fire twined as one at the crown, turning the ritual timetable into the practice of the lights.
2327 promised to make clear அஞ்சனம், the collyrium; 2402 delivers it as a brow-paste that makes the wearer unseen, so the opening's table of contents is honoured at the close.

2349 says one who lusts after prostitutes becomes vain and falls into hell; 2402 offers a paste that makes many courtesans swoon. The conflict stands if the charm is meant for use; it dissolves only if 2402 is read as a boast of power never to be exercised.

2393 blames the siddhas for hiding the sign of the egg and speaking in concealment, and sets this book up as plain; 2404 orders the disciple not to give the book to anyone. Openness and secrecy are both claimed for the same text; the conflict holds unless 2393's charge is only against cipher within a text, not against restricting its readers.

Both make release a matter of the mind knowing with certainty: the Kural's mind that ponders and knows what is need not think of birth again; Agasthiyar's mind subdued by devotion, knowing the state in the whorl, has moksha itself. Agasthiyar adds the yogic place; the Kural does not.
audit_text_issue: Kural 357 base text has உணரான் where commentators read உணரின்.

note: Tirumular sets the learned, the ascetics and the virgins each in their own enclosure and says none knows the Lord's nature; Agasthiyar's Vedic men, each at variance with the other, wail in the streets and none sees the divine state. Both make sectarian learning a sign of not knowing.
audit_text_issue: 2407 line 3 ஒன்றொன்றுக்கு கொன்றை மாறி is corrupt (marker reads ஒன்றுக்கொன்று மாறி).

note: Konganar's man who does not know the standing of pooranam lies, recites crores of mantras and, a mere 'effect guru', robs his disciples; Agasthiyar's crores of thieves beguile with words. The same figure, the teacher as thief, in two works.

Tirumular says people do not know the great Being that swallows body and awareness; Agasthiyar says no one sees where the breath went or the way it came, and only 'he' knows. Both locate the unknowable at the point where body and life part, and both tell the reader to look with awareness rather than scripture.
audit_text_issue: 2079 line 3 (உயிர்அன்று உடலை விழுங்கும் உணர்வை) is unsettled.

note: Tirumular sees the holy form of the cosmos standing like milk in water within the vessel of the body; Agasthiyar says the cosmos becomes the body (அண்டத்திற் பிண்டமாகும்). The image of the macrocosm held in the microcosm is shared; Tirumular's is an experience of bliss, Agasthiyar's a doctrine stated.
audit_text_issue: 2412 lines 6 and 8 (புழுக்கூடு வலைமோ தப்பா, குணவியவா னானக்காற்) are damaged.

note: Pattinathar addresses pooranam as having taken a form that makes the whole cosmos-and-body (அண்டபிண்டம்) atom within atom; Agasthiyar places the self in the atom-space and says the cosmos becomes the body. Both use the Siddhars' compound for the cosmos mirrored in the body.
audit_text_issue: 2412 lines 6 and 8 (புழுக்கூடு வலைமோ தப்பா, குணவியவா னானக்காற்) are corrupt.

note: The Kural sets truth spoken with the heart above austerity and giving; Agasthiyar makes truth the first requirement of being human and closes the run on it, while keeping rites and samadhi in their place below it.

Tirumular lays down the breath measures (sixteen in by the left, sixty-four held, thirty-two out) and says this is the truth; Agasthiyar says that if the mind is set right there is no need to raise the vital air or halt the vaasi. The conflict holds if Agasthiyar means the breath practice is dispensable; if he means a right mind already does what the practice aims at, the verses need not clash.
audit_text_issue: 573 ஓமத்தால் unclear, as the marker notes, but the breath measures are not in doubt.

note: The Kural says a spotless mind is the whole of virtue and everything else is noisy show; Agasthiyar says a right mind is the whole of mantra and the breath practices are unnecessary. The same move, mind made the sole essential and outward means set aside, in ethics and in yoga.

Tirumular says silence is speech and mind both stilled, and that a silent mouth alone is mere muteness; Agasthiyar says the mantra is right when the mind is right, not when it is recited. Both place the practice's worth in the mind's state and not in the act.

Tirumular says that with the two breaths set in the upper palate there is no Death and grey hair and wrinkles reverse; Agasthiyar says those who direct the life-letter upward every day live as long as the earth and escape Death's hand. The same claim of bodily deathlessness by breath practice.

The Naladiyar says no one has leapt clear of Death and escaped, so give while you can; Agasthiyar says the daily practitioner lives as long as the earth and is not caught in Death's hand. The conflict holds if Agasthiyar's claim is about the physical body, as the Siddhars' kaya-siddhi tradition takes it; if 'not caught by Death' means release from rebirth, the two need not clash.
audit_text_issue: Naladiyar 6 line 1 பிழைத்தெரிணஇக் is corrupt (for பிழைத்தொரீஇக்).

note: Sivavakkiyar's mantra that rose as 'a' and 'u', settled as 'a', 'u' and 'm' in the Supreme, is Sivayam; Agasthiyar's sky-light is Om, 'a' and 'u', beyond anyone's reach, and one's life is Siva. Both read the letters of Om as the inner Siva; Sivavakkiyar says the knower has no further birth, Agasthiyar that knowledge is complete.

Tirumular drives bindu and nada upward to drink the nectar, and bindu itself dies; Agasthiyar makes knowing bindu's standing turn nada into the guru and the knower into his own guru. Agasthiyar takes the pair Tirumular uses as a practice and turns it into a doctrine of the inner guru.

Pattirakiriyar asks when he will burn the shastras, make the four Vedas a lie and see the sutra; Agasthiyar says he who burns and throws away the shastras is the siddha. Both make the burning of scripture the mark of the knower rather than a loss.

2406 tells the children to look again and again at the many Vedas and shastras; 2419 says the one who burns the shastras is the siddha. Within the same work the two are incompatible unless 2406 is read ironically (its 'path made for them to live' being the livelihood path 2407 mocks) or as a stage that 2419 leaves behind.

Tirumular states what happens at death: the subtle body, having eaten what is in heaven and hell, goes on as the cause with its old deeds and takes a new body. Agasthiyar says no one has known where the life goes, and that 'joins the sky-Siva' and 'fire joins fire' are the sayings of those who do not know. The conflict holds if Agasthiyar's 'no one' includes the yogic account and not only the popular sayings he lists.

Sivavakkiyar says the Vedas, Agamas, treatises of truth and the teaching tied on (கட்டிவைத்த போதகம்), all the madness fit for stories, ended in nothing once he knew the Lord; Agasthiyar says the ancients tied on (மாட்டினார்) stories, kavyas and Puranas to bewilder. The same verb for scripture as something bound on from outside, and the same verdict.
audit_text_issue: 2422 has seven lines and lacks the antadi opening; இயலான ரசந்தனிலீப் புகுந்தாற் போலும் is obscure.

note: Tirumular says the Lord set by grace, for souls, hell and heaven and endless births, no different from the earth; Agasthiyar says the Vedas and shastras made dharma and adharma, rebirth and noble birth, and that all of it is for livelihood. On a plain reading Agasthiyar denies what Tirumular affirms. The conflict softens only if Agasthiyar attacks the use made of these doctrines and not their truth, which the verse does not say.

The Kural says those who have learned here and seen the true thing reach the path of not coming back, taking rebirth as real and release from it as the goal; Agasthiyar lists 'there is birth' among the things scripture made up for a living. The conflict depends on reading 2425 as denying rebirth rather than as mocking its preachers.

Tirumular says one can guard the four inner instruments, the sixteen kalas and the breath if one stands with the mind fixed; Agasthiyar says that if you set the mind and guard pooranam, which is the sixteen kalas, it becomes the Siva-yoga life called vaasi. Both make guarding the sixteen kalas by a fixed mind the yoga.
audit_text_issue: Tirumanthiram 713 prints கலைபதி நாறையும், a word-split that hides பதினாறு.

note: Tirumular's sun takes in all sixteen kalas of fulfilment through the great breath; Agasthiyar's sixteen kalas are pooranam, the fullness, kept by the vaasi. The sixteen kalas as the breath's fullness is shared; Agasthiyar makes the number itself the definition of God.
audit_text_issue: Tirumanthiram 853 line 2 (நாறா நலங்கினார் ஞாலங் கவர்க்கொள) cannot be construed and the whole verse is read roughly.

note: Tirumular says those who set Nandi in love have no caste, no stain and no pride; Agasthiyar says the knowers of pooranam did silent Siva-yoga, and that caste, 'I' and 'you' were set up for the worldly who trust the body. Both place caste among the things the knower is free of; Agasthiyar adds that it was invented for a living.

The Naladiyar says 'good caste' and 'bad caste' are words with nothing behind them, and that austerity, learning and effort make a lineage; Agasthiyar says caste was set up for livelihood. Both deny caste a real basis, the Naladiyar replacing it with merit and Agasthiyar with knowledge of pooranam.

Sivavakkiyar asks what mantra it is to call a planted stone God and circle it muttering, when the Lord is within, and whether the pot that cooked the curry knows its taste; Agasthiyar says the fools who take stone and copper for God, not knowing pooranam, bark like dogs. The same attack on idols, with the same ground, that God is within.

Tirumular says curd, ghee, milk, copper, fire, mercury, brick, bilva or gold can each be the Sivalinga when clearly known; Agasthiyar says those who take stone and copper for God are fools. The conflict holds on the plain reading of both; it softens if Tirumular's 'clearly known' (தெளிந்து) is the knowledge Agasthiyar says the idol-worshippers lack.
audit_text_issue: 1720 line 4 தென்தியங்கு ஒன்றை is unclear, but the list of materials is not affected.

note: Kakapusundar says that when the mind is driven straight to the uvula it leaps to the suzhumunai and the five elements become one; Agasthiyar says that when the mind is set at the suzhumunai and guarded as one thought, the four and the eight become one. Both make the mind's fixing at the central channel the point where the many become one.

The Thirumular Njanam says the two lights rise and subside in the root of the supreme Siva, and the suzhumunai becomes the pillar and the light that is truth; Agasthiyar says the sun and moon exchange and rise at the suzhumunai and subside within it. The same picture of the two breaths meeting and sinking at the central channel.

Tirumular says the false garb is worn for the sake of eating and only the knower's garb saves; Agasthiyar says he who puts on the garb and talks mouth-knowledge for his belly, begging at every house, is a husk who does not know himself. Both tie the false ascetic's garb to the belly.

Pattinathar addresses pooranam as the one who rose as the left, right and central channels and stood as body and life; Agasthiyar says body, life and pooranam are one, body and life being its foot and head. Both speak of pooranam as that which is the body and the life, not something beyond them.

Tirumular's teacher set the thing to meditate on daily below the crown and above the uvula, with the mouth not opened; Agasthiyar's pati dwells in the uvula within the inner sky, and the place is not to be opened in public. The same body-place and the same secrecy; Agasthiyar names it the suzhumunai and Kailasa.
audit_text_issue: 2438 விதியின்ன விடம் is strange; 1780 பச்சிம திக்கு is a guess.

note: Tirumular says the Lord is not in the mansion, hall, courtyard, temple or holy garb but in the hidden place in the heart of those who have given up longing; Agasthiyar makes Kailasa, Vaikuntha, Kasi, Kumari and Setu names of the inner place of pati. Both relocate the holy place within; Agasthiyar does it by renaming the pilgrimage sites rather than denying them.
audit_text_issue: 2439 காசின்யா and மயிலாடு மேகம் uncertain

note: Kakapusundar tells the disciple to pluck and eat the black gooseberry, which becomes the unboiled head, and to hold the white snake, which is the undying breath; Agasthiyar tells him to stand on the serpent's head, find the undying breath and see the true black-gooseberry juice. The same three cipher images (gooseberry, serpent, undying foot) for the inner kalpa.
audit_text_issue: 2353 கலைநாலு ... எட்டில் is unexplained.

note: Tirumular drives bindu and nada upward along the marked path and drinks the nectar that is milk; Agasthiyar climbs from the serpent's head to the tip and sees the true juice of the black gooseberry. Both make the deathless substance something found by ascent within the body, and both warn that it is lost by letting go.

Sattaimuni tells the disciple to learn Valai's three letters and worship her, then Tripura's eight, Bhuvanai's and Yamalai's; Agasthiyar says the house of turiya is Valai, Nathar-Maheswari, and that she alone is to be worshipped. Both make Valai the object of the inner worship; Agasthiyar identifies her with the fourth state itself.

The Kural opens with 'a' as the first of letters and the Primal Lord as first of the world; Agasthiyar closes 2444 with the Supreme as the first letter. The image of God as the first letter is shared; the Kural uses it as a simile, Agasthiyar as an identity within the Omkara science of 2445.
audit_text_issue: 2444 பாமென்ற is unexplained; the line's sense is uncertain

note: Tirumular says that by one letter he became everything, by two he joined as two, by three the light springs up; Agasthiyar maps 'a' to pati, 'u' to pasu and Om to the Supreme, and tells the disciple to see the letter of light. Both read the letters of Om as the stages of the Lord's manifestation; Agasthiyar's mapping is onto the Siddhanta categories, Tirumular's onto the world.

Arunagirinathar asks to hold the serpent-like breath, see the pure light, plunge into the space above and see the vel and peacock shining there; Agasthiyar says that when the middle nadi is fixed the stream appears, the five dance, and light-space and the sound of anklets are seen as one. Both make the inner light and the vision in the upper space the fruit of the held breath.

2418 says that when nada becomes the guru you yourself become the guru who is beginning and end; 2451 says the guru is he who knows and tells the root that became the three and the two letters, and that the fools who say 'we have known' and even the gods have not seen it. The later run turns the inner-guru claim into a test for judging teachers.
audit_text_issue: 2451 ஊவெழுத்து may be corrupt.

note: Sivavakkiyar mounts the vaasi on the silent five letters and enters the light-filled sphere, where he and the Lord mingle until neither remains; Agasthiyar fixes the fine letter, mounts the good vaasi, crosses to the jewelled hall and looks to the Supreme that is the letter's inner meaning. The same ride of the breath on a mantra to the crown, with release as its fruit.

Tirumular says that though the Agamas are gathered in countless crores, without the knowledge the Lord declared they are writing on water; Agasthiyar says those who have learned the Agamas and many books and claim knowledge cannot answer for the undying head and foot, and only he who sees the one letter in the body is the jnani. Both deny that learning the Agamas is knowing.

The Kural asks what learning has achieved if the learned do not bow at the feet of the one of pure knowledge; Agasthiyar asks what the learners of the Agamas and many books know if they cannot tell the undying head and foot. Both measure learning by a knowledge it does not itself contain.

Tirumular says those who grieved the ascetics who taught the one-syllable mantra will be born as outcast dogs in a hundred forms; Agasthiyar says those who mock this book will live as ghosts in dire hell. The same closing curse on those who slight the teaching of the one letter; Tirumular's punishment is rebirth, Agasthiyar's is hell.

2457 says that leaving yoga for silence gives no siddhi; 2465 restores silence as the life without distinctions that arrives once the breath is sent to the palate and held at twelve. Silence is the fruit of the practice, not a substitute for it.
audit_text_issue: 2457 lines 1-2 (கண்ணாடி சிலமூடித் தனுப்பினாலே) are obscure, possibly corrupt.

note: Sivavakkiyar describes alchemy (வாதம்) as it is practised, a confidence trick with the fee taken and the alchemist fled; Romarishi holds that alchemy is real but unreachable without yoga and without leaving women. The one treats the claim, the other the trade.
audit_text_issue: 2457 lines 1-2 obscure, possibly corrupt.

note: Tirumular has moon and sun rising and falling through ida and pingala with life welling in the middle; Romarishi names the left channel moonstone and the right the sun and makes their union in the middle release itself.

Tirumular seizes the twelve female kalas and the sixteen male kalas and pours them into the fire for bliss; Romarishi draws in at sixteen, holds at twelve and blows, and the eightfold subtle body subsides. The same two numbers, with the sun and moon assigned to them.

Tirumular's unworthy disciple is the one who does not give up lust and does not fear birth and death; Romarishi's unfit disciple is the householder who hears the way to live and does not look at it. Both make fitness a condition of teaching.

Pattinathar says taking to the forest, eating wind and wearing rags gain nothing without inner love; Romarishi says those who climbed hills and ate dry leaves died in crores of the fire of lust. Both deny that bodily austerity by itself reaches the goal.

Both attack the preacher who holds forth: Agasthiyar's men who pore over books, call themselves gurus and shout that they are the Trimurti; Romarishi's talkers who deny body, release and yoga and die of their empty speech.

Tirumular's body made to shine without defect and turn gold by the Siva-water; Romarishi's sign of release with form, the gross body seen like a flame. Both take a shining body as the visible proof of attainment.
audit_text_issue: 2467 அபராட்சம் beside சிரவணம் may be a slip for பராட்சம் (marker's note).

note: Tirumular reckons the span of life from the running of the breath, a hundred years if it runs five, eighty if four; Romarishi reckons it from the day's count of 21,600 breaths and says the days are lost as breaths go out. The same theory of life as a breath budget.

The Kural asks what is stronger than fate, which gets ahead of anything else one devises; Romarishi says fates are only what one has thought, with the god concurring. On the reading that 2468 makes fate the product of thought and not its master, the two claims are incompatible.
Tirumular gives puraka, kumbhaka and recaka their measures; Valmiki keeps the three terms and maps them onto the four Saiva paths, so that the whole of Saiva practice is one breath.

Tirumular sorts the four paths into four kinds of people, with the siddhas at jnana; Valmiki makes them four phases of one breath that every practitioner passes through, and the siddha is the one who joins them.
Sivavakkiyar maps the four paths onto the four states of release; Valmiki maps the same four onto inhalation, retention, exhalation and stillness.
The Kural's hunter hiding in a bush is Valmiki's fruit-eating mute who calls his wandering yoga: austerity worn as cover for what is not austerity.
Tirumular's fools in guises who dance, sing and wail yet never see Siva's feet are Valmiki's book-readers who melt before stone, eat roots and go round like beasts.
Both name the false guru by his trade: Tirumular's has surveyed mantra and yoga yet goes blind for food; Valmiki's dons costumes, takes disciples and gives initiation to make a living.
audit_text_issue: தூடிப்பாருலகத்தல் in line 2 looks garbled.

note: The Kural's cow grazing in a tiger's skin; Valmiki's yogi in matted hair, tiger skin and ash who does not know the cause. The skin marks the pretence in both.
Tirumular wants the king to test those who put on matted hair, tuft and thread and act the wise; Valmiki counts them in crores howling in the forest. Both make the garb empty without knowledge.

Agasthiyar counts both the unseeing wanderers and those who know the cause as crores upon crores; Valmiki, in the same words, says those who have seen the cause are few. On a plain reading of Agasthiyar's second line the counts conflict; it may be hyperbole or a corrupt line.
audit_text_issue: 2431 line 2 may be a copyist's repetition of line 1's கோடாகோடி.

note: Sivavakkiyar asks what caste is when all water is one and the five elements are one; Valmiki says the four castes and the many castes were strung together by men for a living. Both deny caste a natural ground.

The Kural says birth is alike for all and distinction comes from work; Valmiki says caste was made by men to live by. Both refuse birth as a ground of rank, though the Kural keeps a ground in deeds that Valmiki does not mention.

Tirumular: fix both gazes at the middle of the nose and we become Siva. Valmiki: those who have seen Siva at the nose-tip are themselves the three gods. The same place in the body yields the same identity.
Mounachiddhar knows the gaze by the way of the nose-tip and the raising of the vaasi; Valmiki sets seeing Siva at the nose-tip against the word-mongers who do not know the vaasi.
Tirumular: where the abiding mind is, there the breath is. Valmiki: keep the mind at the place where the vaasi arises and the mind enters with it and subsides.

Tirumular says no one knows the measure of the breath drawn in and let out through both nostrils, and that those who know it kick Death; Valmiki says the two breaths are hard for anyone to see and the one who sees them is the Siva-siddha.
Tirumular's Lord tells the secret of release only to those on the path of virtue; Valmiki forbids showing his book to fools. Both guard the teaching by the fitness of the hearer.

The Kural makes understanding the seeing of the true substance of whatever is heard; Valmiki's seeing needs no witness, companion or hearsay. Both place knowledge in direct seeing rather than in report, and Valmiki goes further in dismissing report.
audit_text_issue: 2482 விழியைக் காண and the last line's syntax are uncertain, as the marker notes.

note: Tirumular stayed through the ages keeping a measured diet with mind withdrawn; Valmiki prescribes fruit, the five juices and fine foods in due measure as the guard of the breath-practice.
audit_text_issue: Tirumanthiram 76 lines 2-4 (மிதாசனி / இதாசனி / உதாசனி யாதிருந்தேன்) are not securely construed.

note: Thiruvalluvar Njanam's invocation hails Guhan (Murugan) seated within the kundalini and the lotus of the suzhumunai; here the suzhumunai is the place where the practice subsides and Murugan is present as the Om-vel. In both, Murugan is a resident of the central channel.

note: Tirumular says what the masters attain is two things, Omkara and the five letters; the invocation makes Om, in the shape of the vel, the instrument by which one sees oneself and reaches the supreme void.

note: Tirumular derives Siva and Shakti, and then knowledge and action, from nada and bindu; this verse derives Parasiva, Shakti, the sevenfold creation and the two sons from the sound born of the Supreme.
Arunagiri names Murugan who circled the whole world on his golden peacock before the elephant-faced one and his father; here the contest is set and Murugan leaps on the peacock to round the hill.

Arunagiri praises Ganapati who won the fruit by circling his father; here Ganapati sees that Meru is the parents themselves, circles their feet and takes the mango. The Siddhar text adds the reasoning the hymn only names.
Arunagiri says Murugan taught Agastya the ways of knowledge and penance in Tamil at Palani; here Agastya hails Shanmuga as his guru and the rest of the work is that teaching.

Tirumular's Siva-guru makes the disciple bow, tests him with pure teaching and then shows the real and the unreal; Murugan asks Agastya who he is and why he has come before he teaches, and only then gives the gracious glance.
audit_text_issue: 2497 திரணமதாய் and கரணமந்தக் கரணமதாய் are doubtful.

note: Romarishi gives inhalation, retention and exhalation their counts (four, four, one and three); this verse gives them seed syllables and places, VANG at the root to fill and SING in samadhi to let out. Two notations for the same phases.

note: Agasthiyar makes the suzhumunai the stream and names the Om-science of the letters; here, in the suzhumunai, Om with the seed letters and Om Namasivaya give the vision of Brahman.

note: Both permute the five letters as practice. Tirumular rotates them (SIVAYANAMA, MASIVAYANA, NAMASIVAYA and so on); Subramaniar reverses them head to foot and foot to head. The principle, that the mantra's power lies in its orders, is shared; the operation differs.

note: Tirumular: fix the mind twelve finger-breadths below the nose and the body never decays. Subramaniar: reverse the five letters, meditate, wear ash daily and the unstable gross body becomes stable. Both promise a body made to last by inner practice.

Tirumular: fill the ten nadis, hold prana and apana together, stay still, and there is no Yama for us. Subramaniar: fix the breath, do pranayama, and the diseases called Death run away. The same claim, with Death read as disease.

Tirumular measures the breath: sixteen in by the left, thirty-two out by pingala, sixty-four held between. Subramaniar gives the same three acts, with a fourth place, as syllables at body-stations: VANG at the root, SING in the suzhumunai, ANG at the throat. Counts in one, letters in the other.
audit_text_issue: 573 line 4 ஓமத்தால் is unclear; 2511 கருமானம் is uncertain.

note: Sivavakkiyar's vaasi rises gently on the silent five letters into the filled light, where he and I mingle and no one remains; here the vaasi climbs to the whorl, returns to live in the body, and the practitioner becomes this world and the beyond. Both end the breath's rise in a state past the self.

Tirumular's yogis bind the breath and taste the nectar of knowledge-bliss from the bright moon; Agastya is told to raise the vaasi, stand at the whorl and take the untroubled nectar, which the next verse calls moon-nectar.
The invocation names the vel the shape of Om; here the vel's point is silence and the six-faced station is at the end of sound. The work moves from Om as the vel to what lies past sound at its tip.

Tirumular lists the eight limbs, from yama to samadhi; Agastya is sent to go by the eightfold yoga (அட்டாங்க யோகம்) to the guru's feet. The verse names the discipline and relies on Tirumular's kind of enumeration for its content.

In Tirumular Siva sends Agastya south to stand first in the tilting world; here Murugan sends him to Sathuragiri and Pothigai. The two texts share Agastya's commission to the south, but the sender differs.
The summit of the cosmic bound (அண்டவரை முடி) and the vel shaped as Om (ஓங்கார வடிவேல்) open and close the work; the invocation states the practice and the colophon shows Murugan performing it.

Pattinathar does not know the sign of the form the Lord took as atom within atom in all the cosmos and the body; Valaisami opens his tattva with the one growing as the two, cosmos and body, and then as many kinds. Both make அண்டம் and பிண்டம் the first division of the one.
audit_text_issue: 2522's அண்டபிரண்டம் is probably a misprint for அண்டபிண்டம்.

note: The Naladiyar's body is a pot seeping filth from nine openings that only a fool calls beautiful; Valaisami's body is a vessel of filth too, but he names it only to ask what subtle thing enters it and where that comes from. The same image serves disgust in one and inquiry in the other.
audit_text_issue: 2523: சிற்பனம், உற்பனம் are irregular forms, and the line may be corrupt.

note: Pattinathar's picture 'matching ten and eight, two fives, thirteen, two and one' and Valaisami's five villages divided five by five from one seed both give the tattvas as a number-cipher the hearer must decode; neither names a single tattva.
audit_text_issue: 2529 is run together and obscure (ஆணகுளம் unclear).

note: Tirumular places fire, water, air, sun, moon and the gods all within the heart; Valaisami's space-light says the share of the five is gathered within himself. In both the elements are held inside one inner principle rather than outside the body.

Tirumular gives the breath in counts by channel: in by the left, out by pingala, held between. Valaisami gives the same single breath moving through three channels as one ox drawing one plough through three furrows, a farm riddle in place of a count.

Tirumular makes the heart the great temple, the flesh the shrine and the mouth the tower gate; Valaisami makes the body a Siva temple with the head as tower and, in the following stanzas, the uvula as flagstaff and the palate as tank. Both read temple architecture onto the body, Valaisami in more anatomical detail.
audit_text_issue: 2555 line 3 (காகமன விரண்டு கரக்கோடுங் கையாம்) is damaged.

note: Sivavakkiyar scolds those who worship temples and tanks: the temple and the tanks are in the mind. Valaisami keeps the temple and the tanks but relocates them into the body, head, uvula and palate; the one abolishes the outer temple, the other translates it.
audit_text_issue: 2555 line 3 is damaged.

note: Sivavakkiyar's mutes pity the whirling gate without thinking to open it and perceive the truth; Valaisami's wanderers cannot find the temple's gate and he gives the key, the silent letter that opens the way to the crown. Both make the opening of an inner gate the whole task.
audit_text_issue: 2562 line 1 is garbled.

note: Tirumular locks the breath in the body as with a bolt and turns the gaze within; Valaisami's lock on the holy gate is opened by the letter of silence. Both treat the practice as a matter of locks and bolts, one closing the breath in, the other opening the gate up.
audit_text_issue: 2562 line 1 (அக்ஷரமாமௌனாக்ஷாமா மது / வானால்) is garbled; முத்திதமாக is uncertain.

note: Tirumular's three voids where words cease give the experience at the end of the three; Valaisami asks whether the hearer has first crossed the three voids and finds three lights within the presence. Both place the final seeing past a threefold emptiness.
audit_text_issue: 2570 றரத்துவம் is a misprint for தத்துவம்; 2483 line 2 is obscure.

note: Tirumular puts the Lord's dwelling three or four finger-breadths from the tip of the nose, past the Veda's reach; Valaisami puts the suzhumunai at the nose-tip and the guru Nandi in the circle of light there. Both locate the Lord at the nose's point rather than only at the brow or crown.

Tirumular gazes steadily between the brows and takes the place where the Supreme sits as the little hall; Valaisami's fixed mark is the gaze at the brow-centre, where sun and moon stand and Nandi sits. The same gaze at the same place, with the hall and the fire-circle as its names.

Sivavakkiyar asks the gnanis to explain how the fourfold womb and bindu settle in the banyan seed and arise from the womb; Valaisami answers in the same terms, that the four wombs and the seven births are nada and bindu, and body and life come from them.
audit_text_issue: போனி in both is a misprint for யோனி; 2573 line 1 (தச) is damaged.

note: The Subramaniar Njanam has the two letters and the one letter moving as the ajapa in the root, sprouting from the seed-letter; Valaisami gives A at the kundalini-breath, the next letter at the throat and M at the whirl. Both distribute the letters of Om along the body's rise.
audit_text_issue: 2578 has அகாரம் twice; the second (at the throat) is probably உகாரம்.

note: Tirumular fixes puraka at sixteen, kumbhaka at sixty-four and rechaka at thirty-two, and says to change the order in any of these is deceit. Valaisami gives puraka thirty-two and rechaka sixteen, reversing the intake and release while keeping the hold. If Valaisami's numbers are his and not a corruption, the two prescribe incompatible breath counts, and Tirumular's own rule condemns the change.
audit_text_issue: The kummi's counts may be transposed.

note: Tirumular breathes in by the left and out by pingala with the hold between; Valaisami places the puraka in the left and the rechaka in pingala, held 'in Nandi'. The channel assignment is the same in both.

Tirumular's Siva-yogis kindle the fire, turn it back and raise it, and drink step by step the nectar of the full moon; Valaisami raises the fire with the breath, carries it above the whirl and feeds it nectar. The same sequence of fire raised and nectar tasted.

Tirumular ranks Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra, Maheshvara and the five-faced one, with Sadasiva common to all; Valaisami assigns the same five, in the same order, to the five letters NA MA SI VA YA. The hierarchy of gods in one is the structure of the mantra in the other.
audit_text_issue: 2585 கிவ்வெழுது is a misprint for சிவ்வெழுத்து.

note: Sivavakkiyar holds that within the five letters are the cosmos and what is beyond it and the three gods, everything contained; Valaisami says the moving and the unmoving are sustained by the faultless five letters. Both make the mantra the container of the world.

Sivavakkiyar tells devotees that the five letters and the three letters are not the thing itself. Valaisami keeps the maiden's three letters as the key but says no mouth can speak them and they are made by joining three places in the body; he moves the letters past utterance rather than denying them.

Tirumular's king should punish those who drink liquor instead of the nectar taken by binding the breath, raising the fire and holding the moon's face; Valaisami tells the dancers not to drink toddy or sleep on ganja but to feed on the moon's drink from within. The same substitution of inner nectar for intoxicants.

Pattinathar asks when, not drinking ganja, opium and toddy, he will drink the fivefold nectar; Valaisami tells the dancers to refuse toddy and ganja and feed on the Soma-digit's drink. Both set a nectar above the Siddhar intoxicants.

Tirumular lists Virat, Hiranyagarbha and Avyakrita as the presiding selves under the 'that' of the great saying; Vaalaisami stacks the same three with consciousness above them, and chapter 141 will assign them to the Supreme's waking, dream and sleep.
audit_text_issue: 2610: இண்டமுண்ட is garbled. Tirumanthiram 2537: the third group of names is garbled.

note: Tirumular maps 'thou', 'that' and 'art' onto pasu, pati and sayujya, keeping the Siddhanta triad whole. Vaalaisami redefines the same triad from the Vedanta side: pasam the body, pasu the soul, and love standing where pati stood. Same three words, two systems of reference.

Both make the breath a horse with twelve legs (ஈராறு கால் and காலோ பன்னிரண்டு), legs being winds, and both say it must be tied fast; Tirumular promises long life from the binding, the kummi only that the horse comes under measure.
audit_text_issue: 2614 அச்சு மட்டம் is obscure (மட்டம் may be a pony).

note: Tirumular's two horses come under control only by the guru's grace, since no one knows the skill to catch them; Vaalaisami gives the technique, binding at the lowest gate by kundalini's vaasi, and sends the hearer to the great ones elsewhere (2600, 2604) rather than here.
The enemy knocking at the mind's fort is unnamed here; the next part opens by naming him Kama, eldest of all, and counts his brothers, children and friends to thirteen.

Sivavakkiyar's monkey mind swells here and there while millions say 'the One'; Vaalaisami's monkey is possessed by a ghost and revels. Both make the restless mind the obstacle to a practice named by a syllable, and the kummi adds a medicine for it.
audit_text_issue: 1294 line 1 (ஆகிகூவென்று) and பூகமாய் are obscure, possibly corrupt.

Both describe the outfit (matted hair, ochre, beads, ash) of men who call themselves yogis and jnanis; Vaalaisami adds the beard and the word சந்நியாசி, and asks who will accept them, where the other poet says they roam not knowing the cause.

Vaalaisami divides gurus into word-gurus who lie and sat-gurus whose word is to be heard. Sivavakkiyar lists word-gurus, true gurus and sat-gurus in one breath and calls all of it gathered impurity. On the dismissive reading of 1014 the two cannot both hold: one says join the sat-guru, the other that the rank is no purer than the rest.

note: Arunagirinathar says what is sought does not come by mercury and the like, the nine metals put to charcoal; Vaalaisami asks whether gold grows from mercury and sulphur in a crucible. note: Here the alchemy becomes khechara when the seed-syllable is known; in the next part khechara is named the non-dual Brahman that the hearer is to reach, past even the regulated breath. The alchemical term is carried over into the Vedantic goal.

note: Tirumular's five-hooded serpent fills the anthill of enjoyment until its hoods fold into one; Vaalaisami's snake lies in the anthill as the world's bond lies in the heart. Both house a serpent in the body's mound, Tirumular to show the senses drawn in, the kummi to show a danger hidden until bluster is subdued.

note: Valluvar says neither the shaven head nor long hair is needed if one gives up what the world condemns; Vaalaisami asks who will accept the beard, matted hair and sannyasi costume of one who runs about in base antics. Both strip renunciation of its outward marks and judge it by conduct.

Tirumular's false gurus have looked over mantra, yoga and jnana without reflecting on them and teach for their food; Vaalaisami's word-gurus tell lies and cannot free anyone. Both define the false guru by words without inner knowledge, and both keep the true guru as the remedy.
audit_text_issue: 2633 line 2, தங்க இறவமோ, is corrupt.

note: Both describe the alchemist-guru who announces a transmutation and walks off with the client's money; Valaisami names such men false gurus, the other poem tracks them a league away. The Siddhars' quarrel with alchemists is first about fraud.
audit_text_issue: 2644 lines 1-2 (திருசுசுன்னம், வெட்டாரை) are partly corrupt.

note: The Kural calls hardest of heart those who live by deceit while seeming to have renounced; Valaisami's false gurus, who talk of the substance and take money, are that type in an alchemist's dress.

Both make salt the alchemist's secret and place it within: the other verse says that of the many kinds of rock salt the true one is in the inner mind; Valaisami says the alchemist is simply the one who knows the salt.
audit_text_issue: 2648 line 3 (பூமி நாதமகிமை) is obscure.

note: The black gooseberry, the Siddha kalpa herb, appears in both: there as something to pluck and eat so the head will not burn, here as already growing in the house, so that no trip to the Kolli hills is needed. The second reads the first's herb as cipher.
Both attack the ascetic who smokes ganja and passes for an eater of kalpa; Valaisami adds that going to caves and mountains does not change what such men can know.

In the same kummi, 2593 makes kundalini's vaasi at the root triangle the knowing itself; 2657 counts doing the vaasi by rechaka, puraka and kumbhaka as desire. On the reading that the vaasi is meant in both, the song first prescribes and then dismisses the practice; the conflict dissolves only if the measured pranayama of 2657 is distinguished from the vaasi of 2593.
audit_text_issue: 2593 வாகியினால் probably for வாசியினால்; நியாபம் unclear.

note: Tirumular gives the measures of puraka, kumbhaka and rechaka (sixteen, sixty-four, thirty-two) and calls any change of the order deceit; Valaisami calls doing the vaasi by rechaka, puraka and kumbhaka mere desire. One makes exact breath-counting the truth, the other an attachment to be left for the non-dual Brahman.

The gate in the gate, with its small gate, recurs almost verbatim from the temple section of the kummi; there one looks at the tight lock, here one closes the small gate oneself, and the image now stands among the observances rejected as desire, as the one that is not.

note: Tirumular says the holy waters are within the heart and those who do not bathe there wander over hill and hollow; Valaisami counts Ganga bathing and puja as desire. Both move the tirtha inward.

note: The other verse asks whether karma leaves at Kasi or with bathing in the Ganga; Valaisami answers the same question by naming the bathing as desire, and adds sect difference to the list.

note: Tirumular calls the Veda and the Agama the two the Lord spoke, which in due order become Vedanta and Siddhanta; Valaisami tells the girl to shut up the holes of Veda and sastra, yet two stanzas later takes up Vedanta and Siddhanta 'by the Siddhars' word'. note: If நாலேழு is read as twenty-eight, Valaisami's count of tattvas matches Tirumular's twenty-eight, twenty-three with prakriti plus turiya, time, the void and the higher turiya. The agreement rests on the numeral reading.

note: In 2610 the kummi named Avyakrita, Hiranyagarbha and Virat with consciousness above them; here it explains them as the Lord's owners of waking, dream and deep sleep, matched to the jiva's Visva, Taijasa and Prajna.

note: Tirumular lists after the supreme waking a dream that has eaten the world, deep sleep and upasanta, and makes reaching them the bearing of Siva's turiya; Valaisami names the same set, supreme waking, the world-devouring and the upasanta, as Siva's states. The kummi is following the Tirumanthiram's Saiva extension of the avasthas.

note: Tirumular distinguishes the soul's turiya, the Supreme's turiya and Siva's turiya and matches them to tvam, tat and asi; Valaisami's three tiers end the same way, with the jiva's states, the Lord's states and Siva's turiya in which identification is lost.

Both place the goal past turiya itself: the other verse says 'beyond even turiya, far, far, far'; Valaisami calls it the turiya never seen, above all three tiers of states, and names it Brahman-bliss.
audit_text_issue: 2690 முற்றிரியம் is likely corrupt.

note: Both make 'thou art that' a knowing rather than a formula: Tirumular's unwearied knowing of soul and Supreme as one is the saying itself; Valaisami's 'tvam' pada becomes the foot that is the 'tat' pada, and the differences, adjuncts and states are all it.

Kakapusundar's opening makes the sects themselves forms the One shows; Valaisami says one's own sankalpa and vikalpa and the sects all became one's own nature. Both absorb the religions into the One instead of refuting them, which softens the Siddhars' usual attack on samayam.

The Meynjanap Pulambal asks when we shall know the joy a mute who dreamed cannot tell; Valaisami says of the Brahman state that there is neither telling it nor hearing it. Both put the goal outside speech from both sides, speaker and hearer.
audit_text_issue: 2697 தாரார் is unclear.

note: Arunagiri's string of negations includes a life that has no distance in space; Valaisami says of the Brahman state that there is no far and no farther. Both deny distance to what is sought, so that seeking cannot be a journey.
audit_text_issue: Thiruppugazh 976 has an encoding glitch (று¡ர for தூர); வீசம் may be a measure rather than space.

note: Valaisami asserts that egg and body became void and beyond them the great void, and tells the women to dance in delight at a Brahman that 'is and is not'. Kakapusundar's disciple presses the question this leaves open: when all the eggs become void and Brahman alone stands, where are the lives, the siddhas and the Trimurti? The kummi gives no answer.

The void beyond the void: Pattinathar's three voids become void and the first void bare void, with the Lord dancing beyond; Valaisami's egg and body become void and beyond the cutting-off is the great void. In both the series of voids ends not in nothing but in what is beyond them, there a dancer, here the Parapara Brahman.
